case_title: SANJEEV KUMAR GUPTA v. STATE OF U.P. (NOW STATE OF UTTARAKHAND)
aggravating_circumstances: Common intention to kill, use of deadly weapons, unlawful assembly
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under Section 302 read with Section 149 of the IPC and sentenced to life imprisonment and fine of Rs.10,000/-
offence_finally_established: Murder under Section 302 read with Section 149 of the IPC
neutral_facts: The accused persons, who were armed with weapons, approached the victim and another individual near a cycle stand at a college campus. They demanded that the victim and the other individual withdraw their names from a college election. When they refused, the accused assaulted them. The victim sustained severe injuries and later succumbed to his injuries. The other individual also received injuries and lodged a complaint with the police. The prosecution presented eyewitness accounts, medical reports, and statements from witnesses to establish that the victim died as a result of the assault. The accused were present at the scene and participated in the attack, with specific roles in causing injuries to the victim. The investigation had some flaws, such as the non-recovery of weapons and delayed recovery of a blood-stained shirt, but the medical evidence and testimonies of the prosecution witnesses supported the prosecution's case. The accused were found to have formed an unlawful assembly with the common object of preventing the victim from contesting the election, and the circumstances indicated that a common intention to kill may have arisen on the spur of the moment.
